title: Thyatira (Revelation 2:18–29)
hookLine: their latest works are more than their first

lines: EYES LIKE A FLAME OF FIRE.
cards: By a riverside outside the city of Philippi, Paul sits down with some women who have gathered to pray. One of them, Acts says, is "a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira."
A businesswoman far from home. She listens, and the text says the Lord opened her heart. Her home town is today's word.

Revelation's next letter goes to its church, and the voice is fierce: eyes "like unto a flame of fire," feet like fine brass. You'd brace for a scolding. Instead, the first thing he says is a compliment worth framing.

teach.h: THE LAST MORE THAN THE FIRST.
teach.b: First, the praise: "I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first." Charity is the King James word here for love.
Ephesus heard that it had left its first love. Thyatira hears the reverse: what they do now is more than what they did at the start. Second, the trouble.
They put up with a teacher the letter calls "that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess." It doesn't give her real name.

Jezebel reaches back to the queen in the book of Kings, wife of King Ahab, who served Baal. The complaint is about what she taught: eating food sacrificed to idols, and what the letter calls fornication.
Even here there's patience: "I gave her space to repent."
Third, a word to everyone who didn't follow that teaching: "I will put upon you none other burden. But that which ye have already hold fast till I come." No new load. Keep hold of what you've got.

teach.h: I WILL GIVE HIM THE MORNING STAR.
teach.b: Fourth, the promise: "And I will give him the morning star," a light that shows before dawn. So Thyatira has a real problem in its middle, and still the first thing heaven says to it is that it's growing.
The letter doesn't treat growth as a peak you hit at the start and slide down from. It can keep going, a little more each season.

how: Christians speak of growing in faith over a lifetime, and some make a habit of looking back over each day in prayer to notice what went well and what could be done better tomorrow.

games.q: you're writing to a church that is growing in love and faith, but has a teacher in its middle leading people astray. what's the first thing you say?
o: praise their growth: the last more than the first.
tell them to start over from scratch.
games.why: the letter opens with praise: "the last to be more than the first." the warning comes after.

practice: Let yesterday play back slowly and stop it at one ordinary moment you'd do a little differently: a short answer to someone, a meal eaten standing up, a chance to help that went by.
Picture today's version, one notch better, done with a bit more care. If you pray, offer that moment to God and ask for help with it; if not, just hold the picture and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Thyatira. Lydia's home town, and the church told that its latest works were more than its first, even with a real problem in its middle.

orig.note: Greek: love. the word the King James renders 'charity' in Revelation 2:19.

carryVoice: Your line: more than at first. Growth doesn't have to peak at the start. Go gently.
